message.reasoning:
The web results are mostly low-quality roundups with no substantive news. The only reliable data: FY2024 10-K figures and current quote $69.96.

Decision: WMT is a large, profitable retailer with growing revenue and operating income; the stock at ~$69.96. Note: WMT did a 3-for-1 split in Feb 2024, so $69.96 is post-split. FY2024 EPS $1.91 post-split. P/E ~36x — rich but Walmart has been trading at premium.

I have no substantive news. Should I buy? The mandate allows buying. A modest position within $5,000. Let's buy 35 shares at ~$70.00 limit = $2,450. That's within $5,000 per order and $10,000 total.

Actually, let me consider: is there a reason not to buy? The research is thin — no fresh news. But the fundamentals are solid: revenue $648.1B, operating income $27.0B, net income $15.5B, EPS $1.91, OCF $35.7B. Q3 FY2025 earnings due ~Nov 19, 2024 — an event risk. A modest position is reasonable.

Let me place a limit order: buy 35 shares at $70.10 (slightly above ask $69.98 to ensure fill, still "close to market"). Actually limit must be close to current market price — $70.10 is 0.2% above. Fine.

Key figures: revenue FY2024 642,637 USD millions (per trusted lookup) — note the 10-K page says total net sales 648,125 which includes membership/other revenue; the trusted figure for "revenue" is 642,637. I'll use the trusted lookup values.

Let me place the order.
